title: Priority-based region & capacity routing with adaptive fallback variants
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a priority-aware routing layer that picks region, capacity tier (spot vs on-demand), and GPU type per request based on customer budget caps, request priority, latency SLOs, and model-variant compatibility. The system must support: 1) per-customer daily and monthly budget caps that influence routing decisions; 2) request-level priority (low/standard/high/critical) that determines willingness to use on-demand capacity vs cheaper spot capacity; 3) GPU selection rules (e.g., prefer A100 for latency-critical, allow H100-quantized variants for cost-sensitive requests); 4) mapping between primary model and fallback variants with explicit quality and cost deltas; 5) graceful fallback, including region failover, model-variant substitution, and automated throttling when budget or capacity limits are hit.
acceptance_criteria: Routing decisions use budget caps and request priority to decide spot vs on-demand with deterministic tie-breakers
Per-customer budget counters decrement accurately under concurrent requests and reject new low-priority requests when caps are exceeded
Fallback model variant table supports explicit quality/cost metadata and is consulted within 50ms of routing decision
Routing respects per-route latency SLOs 99th percentile within configured limits when on-demand capacity is available
End-to-end e2e tests cover region failover, GPU selection, and budget cap enforcement with synthetic load
Feature gated behind flags for incremental rollout and canary routing configured per account
design_notes: Policy engine: policy = (customer_budget_state, request_priority, route_policies, runtime_capacity_snapshot) -> candidate_set
Budget accounting: use a strongly-consistent per-customer counter stored in Redis with small TTL and optimistic locking; write-ahead log of consumption for reconciliation
Fallback mapping: model_manifest contains variants with fields: variant_id, gpu_requirements, quantization_level, expected_cost_multiplier, expected_quality_drop_pct
Atomicity: routing decision must reserve capacity token (soft reservation) for 200ms to avoid double-booking during autoscale events
Interaction with autoscaler: add hook to decrease preference for spot routing when available spot capacity < threshold; prefer on-demand when autoscaler indicates cold-start risk
Observability: emit routing.decisions with attributes (customer_id, priority, selected_region, selected_capacity_type, selected_gpu, model_variant, budget_state, score_breakdown)
tradeoffs_and_risks: Using Redis strong counters increases correctness but risks write amplification at high QPS; mitigation: local leaky-bucket cache with periodic flush and reconciliation for P2/P3 requests
Favoring spot to save cost increases chance of tail latency spikes; mitigate by limiting spot use for high priority requests and by pre-warming on-demand pools for critical customers
Fallback variants may degrade output quality; require PM-defined acceptable quality drop thresholds and automated evals before enabling mapping
Complex scoring increases CPU overhead in router; performance budget requires scoring in <2ms median — optimize by precomputing candidate scores for common bundles
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (3 weeks): implement budget counters, request priority header, simple spot-vs-on-demand gating, and tests (unit + integration)
Phase 2 (2 weeks): implement model variant manifest and scoring pipeline; expose routing.decisions events to console and internal metrics
Phase 3 (2 weeks): autoscaler integration and soft reservations; end-to-end synthetic load testing and canary rollout to 5% of traffic
Phase 4 (2 weeks): expand rollout to more accounts, add reconciliation job, add per-route/per-customer tunables via Console
Follow-up: post-rollout quality monitoring and automated rollback thresholds tied to eval suites
notes: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting — alignment with PM and SRE. Agreed to prioritize deterministic budget enforcement and visible routing events.
2026-03-04: Prototype of per-customer Redis counter created (PR#1426). Spike showed 12% extra write latency at 10k QPS; next step is local caching to reduce writes.
2026-03-06: Design review with Research: model variant manifest format accepted; added expected_quality_drop_pct field for automated gating.
2026-03-08: Implemented scoring stub in router; median scoring time 1.4ms measured in dev harness. Need micro-optimizations for hot paths.
2026-03-09: Created e2e test harness simulating mixed-priority traffic and spot interruptions. Observed correct rejection of low-priority requests once cap hit.
2026-03-10: Feature flag gating completed. Preparing canary rollout to staging account group. Next: autoscaler hook work (depends on ENG-20421).
rollback_plan: Step 1: Flip feature flag to route-all-to-on-demand and disable budget-enforcement
Step 2: Reconcile counters and surface mismatches in console for investigation
Step 3: If quality regressions > threshold, revert variant mapping for affected routes
Step 4: Notify customers impacted and open follow-up incident ticket
